proposal: The Mandate recommends that the CFTC replace its existing position limits rule, which the chapter says reduces liquidity and raises volatility, with further delegation to exchanges to set position limits and accountability levels where appropriate. sources.title: Order Sunsetting Certain Large Trader Reporting Requirements for Physical Commodity Swaps
Swap Execution Facility Order Book Requirement for Permitted Transactions

status_summary: No CFTC proposal or order replacing the federal position limits rule with exchange delegation was found; a final order published 2026-07-21 (91 FR 45638) sunsets routine large trader reporting for physical commodity swaps and leaves the Part 150 position limits in place. CFTC staff gave no-action relief on 2025-07-30 (letter 25-24) from the swap execution facility (SEF) order book requirement for permitted transactions, and the Commission proposed on 2026-08-26 (91 FR 55030, comments closed 2026-09-25) to codify that relief by amending 17 CFR 37.3(a)(2). The order book requirement was adopted in the 2013 SEF core principles rulemaking, but the proposal describes it as a minimum trading functionality requirement and states that it does not change the SEF core principles or SEF registration requirements, so it is at most a narrow step toward the Mandate's call to reduce prescriptive rules.

timeline.event: CFTC staff issued no-action letter 25-24 giving relief from the SEF order book requirement for permitted transactions (as described in the 2026-08-26 proposal).

The CFTC published a proposed rule (91 FR 55030) amending 17 CFR 37.3(a)(2) so that SEFs must offer an order book only for required transactions, not permitted transactions, codifying staff letter 25-24; the proposal states it does not change the SEF core principles; comments closed 2026-09-25.

title: Replace CFTC position limits with exchange delegation; trim core principle rules
uncertainties: Federal Register searches for position limits and core principles since 2025-01-20 were scanned by title (a Federal Register API listing of CFTC documents mentioning position limits returned only an information collection notice bearing on the topic), so a relevant item may have been missed. The large trader order is cited only as context because it does not move the position limits recommendation. Whether the SEF order book proposal counts as trimming rules that implement the core principles is a judgment: the requirement originated in the 2013 core principles rulemaking, but the proposal itself says it does not change the core principles.
